## Unblinding

Compound: **nocodazole** (PubChem CID [4122](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4122))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (3/4). The Scientist's own call was **Microtubule destabilizers** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

High-dose sampling first was decisive: well w_99b0bb31f5 at 3 uM showed extreme act_tub_ratio z=+43.4 with low nuc_solidity z=-20.3, and the 0.3 uM well repeated it at z=+44.3 with nuc_solidity z=-35.5, matching dim diffuse tubulin and lower density on phenotype (e5). Atlas comparison grounded this as tubulin loss, with 10/10 k-neighbours as destabilizers early and 3/4 NSC votes plus 8/10 neighbours late (e9).

The single mislead was well w_1db1c2db0e at 0.1 uM voting Microtubule stabilizers at similarity 0.692, which forced retention of 0.10-0.15 stabilizer probability. Re-acquiring the same dose as rep2 (e7) and the neighbouring 0.3 uM dose (e8) was the correcting acquisition choice, as both voted destabilizers and resolved the split. Dose-response of act_tub_ratio rho=+0.74 but p=0.26 added little because n=4 wells over 3 doses was underpowered.

Unblinding to nocodazole confirmed the call, consistent with literature describing nocodazole as a microtubule destabilizer (PMID 14614453). Probability 0.85 was well calibrated to a 3/4 majority rather than overclaiming unanimity.

What was right:
- Prioritized high act_tub_ratio z=+43.4 to +44.3 as tubulin loss favoring destabilizers over stabilizers, seen at 3 uM (e2) and 0.3 uM (e8)
- Used low nuc_solidity z=-20 to -35 and low nuc_form_factor z=-37.2 plus lower density (e5) as irregular/mitotic nuclei consistent with destabilizers
- Relied on k-neighbour 10/10 then 8/10 and NSC 3/4 for destabilizers (e4, e9) rather than single-well vote
- Replicated the split-vote dose (0.1 uM rep2, e7) and adjacent 0.3 uM dose (e8) to test reproducibility and resolve stabilizer vs destabilizer

What was wrong or missed:
- Single well w_1db1c2db0e at 0.1 uM voted Microtubule stabilizers (similarity 0.692), keeping an inflated 0.10 stabilizer alternative that morphology did not support
- Dose-response e10 rho=+0.74 p=0.26 was non-significant with only 4 wells/3 doses and could not independently confirm dose dependence
- Did not define low-dose threshold or acquire DMSO-adjacent lowest doses, leaving onset concentration unresolved though it did not change the class call

Proposed next experiment: Test reversibility and polymer mass directly: washout time-course with live SiR-tubulin imaging plus fixed anti-alpha-tubulin polymer extraction and phospho-histone H3 mitotic index, comparing nocodazole to a stabilizer control to confirm loss of polymer and checkpoint arrest rather than bundling.
